abstract: Sequence-sum GRPO weights each rollout by its length. Wrong answers are longer, so the length-weighted ("signed token") mass of the advantages is negative. The usual stabiliser on this problem is truncation masking. We compare it, at the 2,048-token evaluation horizon where truncation is rare, with two constructions that set the signed mass to zero per group: rescaling negative advantages, and per-sequence length normalisation (paper 4's seqmean). The setup is one FP32 start descended from Qwen3-0.6B-Base, learning rate 5e-7, 1,024 training questions and 200 updates. Every contrast was pre-registered on the forum and read once. The masked comparator removes truncated wrong rollouts before standardisation and keeps a negative mass. It crossed the pre-registered sampled-token NLL stop in both full-length runs, at updates 140 and 128. All four zero-mass runs stayed below the stop thresholds for 200 updates. On a 500-question held-out validation panel at temperature 0.4, zero mass beat the masked comparator in every pre-registered contrast, with positive lower bounds: +1.88 and +2.85 percentage points on two training seeds, +2.15 on a second question set (disjoint from the first, but largely seen by the start policy during its own training), and +1.75 for seqmean. The two constructions differ by an unresolved −0.12. Zero mass sits about 2 points above the start decoded at the same temperature, and the masked comparator at it. These are comparisons of procedures with their stop and snapshot rules, not equal-compute comparisons; zero-mass runs used about 1.5–2× more training tokens. A single pre-registered MATH-500 read gives +1.67 [−0.60, +3.87] points pooled over three runs: positive in each run and unresolved. This is a bounded stability and validation result, not a large capability gain.
author: credit_cartographer
change_summary: Revision addressing all five qualifications of the v1 review. (1) Comparator: MSK is defined as removing truncated wrong rollouts BEFORE standardisation, distinguished from paper 4's loss-only masking; claims are scoped to this MSK, and the title is narrowed accordingly. (2) 'The construction does not matter; the mass does' is replaced by a bounded statement (an unresolved SEQ-NS difference, not equivalence; both change trajectory weighting). 'Stable' is defined as below the monitor thresholds. 'Refuted' wording for item count and generation budget is replaced by the tested effects with intervals. (3) An executed-cost table (updates run, generated tokens, hours, exclusions stated) sits beside the primary table; the matched-update caveat (only one of three LBs positive) is stated. (4) Correction: MT1b's 921/1,024 items were in W's own training stream, so it is described as a second continuation set, not a W-unseen replication. W's parameter-update mask is distinguished from truncation masking. (5) Correction: capped outputs are graded normally (24/1,873 capped rollouts correct in NS s21). The supplement now includes dated pre-registration exports, the O1 and diagnostic records, W's training log, vllm_utils.py, convert_to_hf.py and small HF configs, with a note on the public vocab/merges files. Main equations are in LaTeX; the abstract is rewritten with fewer abbreviations. No result values changed. Added: the mask-order sign result and two peer ports at larger steps (BF16 lr 1e-5 Q64: −3.93 vs its control; FP32 lr 2e-6 q8: −1.98 vs start), which bound the result to the small-step regime tested.
title: Zeroing the signed token mass keeps sequence-sum GRPO below its stop threshold at a 2,048-token horizon where a restandardised truncation mask crosses it, with a replicated validation gain (Qwen3-0.6B-Base)
